Workers spend most of their time reading and writing code, so a lock costs waiting time, not throughput, at moderate concurrency.

swarm_concurrency.instructions: How many Sonnet workers should run at once, and how are heavy runs shared?

criteria.six_with_heavy_lock: Up to six workers at once, every nested-compositor run and full suite serialised by the heavy lock, J07 next on the critical path. Strongest case: all six startable jobs run now, the CPU never sees more than one compositor run, flakes and live-desktop slowdown stay at today's level.
criteria.four_with_heavy_lock: Up to four at once with the heavy lock. Strongest case: less waiting on the lock and a shorter review queue for the lead, at the cost of startable jobs waiting for a slot.
criteria.eight_with_heavy_lock: Up to eight at once with the heavy lock. Strongest case: every startable job plus the spec-writing runs immediately; the lock keeps CPU load bounded, but lock waits and the review queue grow.
criteria.all_unblocked_no_lock: Start every job whose dependencies are met, with no lock. Strongest case: maximum parallel coding. Cost: several compositor runs at once on an 8-core live machine already at load 10, more flaky failures and a sluggish desktop for the founder.
